title: According to and In Line With

sections.content:
You know *según* + source from B1 Unit 13, *estar de acuerdo con* from B1 Unit 18 and *conforme* as a time word ("as") from B2 Unit 2. This lesson adds two ways to cite or to follow something:

• *de acuerdo con*: "according to". It names a source, such as a person, a report or data: *de acuerdo con el informe*. It can replace *según* in most sentences and sounds a little more formal.
• *conforme a*: "in line with". It says that an action follows a rule, a plan or an instruction: *conforme a la ley*, *conforme al reglamento*. It does not report what someone thinks.

So you choose by what the phrase does: *según* and *de acuerdo con* point to where information comes from; *conforme a* says what an action follows. Remember *a* + *el* becomes *al*.

sections.title: Source or rule?
rows: Según mi jefe, la reunión empieza a las diez.
According to my boss, the meeting starts at ten.
De acuerdo con los datos, hay más turistas que el año pasado.
According to the data, there are more tourists than last year.
Conforme a la ley, todos los empleados deben tener un contrato.
In line with the law, all employees must have a contract.
Hicimos el pago conforme a lo que decía el contrato.
We made the payment as the contract said.

sections.content: You will often hear *de acuerdo a*, but careful writing uses *de acuerdo con*, the same *con* as in *estar de acuerdo con*. After *conforme*, the *a* is not optional: *conforme a la ley*.
